text:
alex: FYI customer 'SparkDocs' hitting sustained 429s from their Dedicated pool during their nightly ingest. Started ~01:05 UTC, ~10m windows of repeated 429s every 5s for many clients. Not seeing obvious spike in request count in their app logs, seems bursty from many pods.

maria: Can you paste the response headers from one of the 429s? We need x-... headers to see which limiter triggered.

alex: Pasting one response we got from their dev environment:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2026 01:07:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-reserved-pool: pool-us-east-1-prod-42
x-rw-pool-capacity: 350000
x-rw-pool-usage: 349890
x-rw-request-cost: 720
retry-after: 5
x-request-id: rwd-381239
```

alex: Their client shows a steady stream of small jobs but concurrency spikes when their cron kicks off, so per-request cost high due to long context length.

sre_jordan: That x-rw-pool-usage almost at cap -> pool cap is being hit, not token rate limit. Looks like reserved-pool token exhaustion.

devin: Agreed. Two levers: reduce per-request cost (truncate context / switch to a cheaper model variant) or increase reserved capacity. Also consider enabling short-term burst headroom if they have that add-on.

maria: @samir can you check if the customer's rollout config pins a heavy model (e.g., 70B) for their bulk job? If so suggest a canary to a quantized 13B for batch ingest.

samir: Confirmed—batch job uses model-id: redwood-70b-latest in their pipeline. They could switch to redwood-13b-q4 for the nightly job with minimal quality impact.

alex: Customer asked for repro steps so they can test: 1) run their nightly cron with HEADLESS=1 and capture request rate + token cost 2) curl a single example and capture response headers 3) measure tail latency and 429 frequency. Provided them sample curl: 

```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-70b-latest","input":"<long-doc>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

maria: Also asked them to gather console -> Routes > Pools > pool-us-east-1-prod-42 -> "Capacity usage (24h)" screenshot and share exact timestamps for spikes.

eng_oncall_bot: New escalation created: ESC-2026-0311-142. Assigned to eng-runtime/capacity. SLA impact: potential degradation for Dedicated customers on pool-42.

sre_jordan: Short mitigation we can propose now: 1) apply per-account soft throttling to their API key to smooth the cron (rate_limit: 120 qps -> 60 qps with 10s token refill) 2) enable 5-minute burst allowance if account has burst feature 3) temporary soft-provision +20% reserved tokens while we observe.

samir: Billing note: increasing reserved capacity affects commitments. Looping @billing_bot.

billing_bot: Heads up: temporary +20% reserved capacity for account sparkdocs will incur overage charges at on-demand rate. We can issue a pro-rated invoice or convert to short-term reservation if they approve.

devin: For long-term: suggest adding work-queue smoothing in their infra (stagger cron across pods) and add lightweight local dedup cache to reduce repeated overlapping requests. Also add model-switch in their pipeline: if job.size > 20k tokens, route to cheaper model.

alex: Customer accepted three-step plan: A) implement model-switch and stagger cron (they'll deploy a canary), B) we provision +20% temp capacity for 4 hours, C) run repro and send console screenshots.

maria: Action items: @samir provision temp cap (ETA 15m), @alex collect console screenshots, @devin prepare a snippet for model-switch policy they can paste into CI.

samir: Provisioned. Updated pool-us-east-1-prod-42 reserved tokens +20% (ticket ESC-2026-0311-142). Watchdog set to auto-revert in 4h.

alex: After provisioning spike subsided in ~8m, customer reports 429s stopped. They ran repro and attached the before/after headers. Before had x-rw-pool-usage 349890, after peaked at 282k.

maria: Follow-ups: 1) share recommended quantized model list and perf/cost delta. 2) discuss longer-term purchase of larger reserved slab or scheduled off-peak window for big jobs.

sre_jordan: I'll schedule a brief review with capacity team to align SLA wording: we should document how burst headroom is billed and how short-term provisioning works so support can propose it quickly.

alex: Closing notes for thread: customer happy for now, will schedule a call to finalize commitment. Leaving this thread open for 24h for monitoring. :white_check_mark:
